citation.title: Estimation of neutral beam injector power transferred to KSTAR plasmas
citation.authors: Jong-Gu Kwak; J.H. Jeong; S.C. Hong

topic: Post-shot calorimetric rechecking of KSTAR NBI neutral power, including duct scraper loss, stray PF field effects and shared-beamline pressure effects
own_question: How accurately does the NBI power recorded from beam current reflect the neutral power delivered to KSTAR plasma in long-pulse and modulation operation?
actual_method_and_evidence: Water-flow calorimetry on beamline components after long pulses. The calorimetric recheck is described as acceptable when coolant reaches steady state in pulses longer than 20 s. Shot examples: #28679 and #11664 show neutral power down about 8.8% by the end of the pulse, while ion beam power stays roughly constant. The authors attribute this to stray PF fields. Duct scraper loss is reported as under about 5% of neutral power. Beam-box pressure rises after beam switching and persists for about 1 s. Neutron emission and Te are used to categorize performance-degradation cases. The evidence is offline only, from a few shots, with no uncertainty quantification. There is no CES, BES/ECEI, or nowcasting content.
input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant; offline post-shot calorimetry, not online inputs.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite as evidence about CES impurity Ti, BES/ECEI, or nowcasting.
Do not claim NBI power errors cause CES label errors in our dataset.
Do not treat the PF-field attribution as demonstrated physics; it is the authors' interpretation.
Do not generalize to KSTAR 2022 data or our chord.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude by default. It is at most an optional context citation that registered NBI heating power can deviate during long pulses, and only if our paper discusses heating-power covariates, which it does not use.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
